title: First Day Where You Have Been in All the Rooms
summary: Given n rooms labeled from 0 to n-1, you start in room 0.
statement: Given n rooms labeled from 0 to n-1, you start in room 0. Each day, if you've visited room i an odd number of times, you move to a room with a lower or equal number as specified by nextVisit[i]. If you've visited room i an even number of times, you move to (i+1) mod n. Return the first day you've visited all rooms, modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: next_visit has length 2 through 100000 and 0 <= next_visit[i] <= i.
After an odd-numbered visit to room i, go to next_visit[i]; after an even visit, go to (i+1) mod n.
Return the first day every room has been visited, modulo 1000000007.
hints: Before first reaching room i, all earlier rooms follow a deterministic revisit cycle.
Let first[i] be its first day; derive first[i] from returning to next_visit[i-1] and then revisiting i-1 evenly.
The interval from the earlier target’s first visit through room i-1’s first visit is traversed twice, with two transition days, yielding the recurrence.

tests.explanation: The visits are room zero, room zero, then room one, so all rooms have been seen on day two.
The recurrence gives first-visit days zero, two, and six.
